hook: HGTV named the trend; skipped the $26.99 price.

scenes.visual_prompt: Magazine or article headline mockup reading Mixed Metals: Trend of the Year
scenes.voiceover: HGTV named mixed metals, brass, chrome, and nickel together, the kitchen trend of the year.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of a kitchen with a brass faucet, chrome fixtures, and mismatched brushed nickel knobs looking cluttered
scenes.voiceover: What they didn't say is most kitchens already have two of those finishes installed, in the faucet or the lights.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand swapping mismatched knobs for matte black pulls across a row of cabinet doors
scenes.voiceover: The fix isn't adding a third metal, it's picking one finish and using it everywhere.

scenes.visual_prompt: Before and after split screen with the same brass faucet, before showing mismatched knobs, after showing matte black pulls
scenes.voiceover: The same brass faucet suddenly reads as a deliberate choice, not a leftover from a past renovation.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text graphic listing four mismatched finishes with an X mark over each
scenes.voiceover: The outdated look isn't brass, it's three or four finishes with no repeating pattern.

scenes.visual_prompt: Price tag graphic $26.99 overlaid on a finished kitchen photo
scenes.voiceover: One $26.99 pack of matte black pulls is the whole fix.

scenes.on_screen_text: Full mixed-metals math, link in bio
scenes.voiceover: I broke down exactly how to audit your own kitchen for this, link in bio.

caption: HGTV called mixed metals the trend of the year but didn't mention most kitchens already have it, just mismatched instead of intentional. Here's the $26.99 fix. Full post linked in bio.
